In this repo (package `tessel`), the flow is in `src/tessel/views.py`:

1. **`VerbView(View)`** is the class with `get()`/`post()` methods.
   - `VerbView.__init_subclass__` (line 165) scans the subclass for method names such as `get` and `post`. It sets `cls.methods = {"GET", "POST"}`, merging in any base-class `methods`.
2. **`View.to_view_func()`** (line 86) turns the class into a view function.
   - It defines an inner `view(**kwargs)` that creates an instance, either per request or once if `init_every_request = False`.
   - It then calls `instance.run_view(**kwargs)`.
   - It copies `methods` (and related attributes) onto the function, so the URL rule registers only those HTTP methods.
   - I did not see a method named `as_view` anywhere in the repo; `to_view_func` appears to be its replacement.
3. **`VerbView.run_view()`** (line 182) does the per-method routing.
   - It runs `getattr(self, request.method.lower(), None)`, so a POST request calls `self.post(**kwargs)`.
   - If the method is `HEAD` and there is no `head` handler, it falls back to `get` (line 188).

The view function is then registered with `add_url_rule` in `src/tessel/sansio/` and called by the app's request dispatch in `src/tessel/app.py`.
